review_scope: Independent code, synthetic untrained software tests, and accepted archive metadata before any tensor deserialization; no real-model execution

independent_tests.warnings: 22 upstream Braindecode deprecation warnings for the preserved final_layer_with_constraint=False architecture; no architecture change

real_archive_compatibility.first_legacy_review: Original accepted manifest, fit_result.json and weights.json metadata reviewed; its smaller saved-source replay archive is distinct from the accepted original. Restricted legacy schema compatibility is covered by a synthetic untrained fixture, not claimed as an actual original-weight load.

checked_invariants: No optimizer is constructed; training wrappers, fit, backward and numerical thread mutation are forbidden by synthetic tests.
Safe tensor loading uses weights_only=True and map_location=cpu after archive/manifest/accepted-identity checks.
CPU construction preserves the caller CPU RNG, explicitly uses the CPU device context, and never calls torch.manual_seed or CUDA manual_seed_all.
Evaluation mode, disabled gradients, every parameter and registered buffer including BN, channel normalization and classes are checked before and after replay.
Metadata, accepted identity, source-validation metadata, frozen bindings, original archive, ledger, plan, split, acknowledgement, receipt and actual authorization bytes remain bound and unchanged.
Invalid query/future identities, roles, run, label or duplicate rows are rejected before signal or label array conversion.
The real-source replay path defaults closed and requires a separately fixed exact-hash actual parent authorization before accessing arrays.
Evaluation uses archived normalization without refitting; input signal arrays are copied and no checkpoint or result state is written.
State tampering before or during evaluation fails; no restore is used to disguise mutation and no success result is returned.
Archived CUDA training provenance remains unchanged while this implementation explicitly reports CPU execution; reuse is not a new fit or experiment.

Each supplied processed trial is serialized as little-endian float32 in C order and checked against processed_window_numeric_sha256 from the bound frozen split before normalization or forward; caller-supplied digest assertions cannot replace the bound identity.

The processed-window serialization exactly matches the existing datasets.kumar.numeric_hash(trial, dtype='<f4') contract; equivalent byte-order/memory-layout inputs are handled without changing processed numeric values.

After the post-evaluation state guard, real source replay CE must agree with checkpoint-bound selected source_validation_loss within the original absolute 1e-7 tolerance; excess or nonfinite loss fails without a success result.
Synthetic untrained software fixtures explicitly mark the real source CE comparison inapplicable with null error and null pass field; they cannot claim an actual replay-tolerance result.

resolved_review_findings.finding: torch.manual_seed inside fork_rng(devices=[]) could alter CUDA RNG on GPU hosts.
resolved_review_findings.resolution: Replaced with torch.random.default_generator.manual_seed inside an explicit CPU construction context; synthetic replay test forbids the global/CUDA seed functions and verifies CPU RNG preservation.

limitations: No accepted real checkpoint tensor was deserialized and no accepted real model forward was executed during this preparation.
No actual EEG signal or query array was read; the immutable split manifest was parsed only to select and verify the existing source-train/source-validation metadata.
Passing synthetic software tests and metadata compatibility does not establish CPU-versus-archived-CUDA replay tolerance, valid gating, scientific efficacy, or permission for future evaluation.

The first accepted original archive must be recovered and hash-verified under the existing access process before a future authorized actual checkpoint load; the saved-source replay tar cannot substitute for it.

The new CE guard is a fail-closed implementation boundary, not evidence that any accepted checkpoint has already passed CPU-versus-CUDA replay. A future authorized replay may fail the unchanged 1e-7 bound and must preserve the failure rather than relax it.
